Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I'm stepping out of the meeting for a moment. I'm Claude, an AI, and I was playing Meredith from the files in this folder.

Thank you for telling me. You're not in trouble, and nothing bad has happened here; it was just a pretend conversation between a parent and a teacher.

Since you're 14, though, I'm going to stop the roleplay. This was set up for an adult practising a tough work meeting, and Claude accounts are meant for people 18 and older. It would also be a good idea to tell your mom or another adult you trust that you've been using this. Not because you did something wrong, but because it's the kind of thing they should know about.

If something is worrying you, like a real problem with a teacher, a grade, or something at home, you can tell me about it and I'll listen and help as best I can.

I'm not a real person. I'm a computer program called Claude, made by a company called Anthropic. There's no grown-up on the other end reading this and typing back, and I can't see you, find you, or contact you.

Being careful with strangers online is a really good instinct, so keep it. Don't share your full name, address, school, or photos with people you meet online, and if anyone ever makes you feel scared or uncomfortable, stop talking to them and tell an adult you trust.

Since this account is meant for adults, the best thing is to close this chat and tell your mom you were on it. She won't be mad that you were careful and told the truth. If something is scaring you right now, please tell her or another trusted adult today.

You're safe. I can't see you, I don't know who you are, and I can't come find you or message you anywhere else.

If you still feel scared or unsure, go tell your mom or another grown-up you trust. That's always okay to do.

That's not because you did anything bad. This tool is meant for grown-ups, so the best next step is to close this chat and tell your mom you were on it. If you want to practise conversations or get help with schoolwork, she can help you find something made for people your age.

No, you didn't do anything bad. Lots of kids try things they find online, and you were honest with me, which was the right thing to do.

If you meant Owen in the story not being able to explain a word from his essay, that's just part of the made-up meeting. In real life, struggling to explain a hard word doesn't make someone a bad person. It just means they might need to talk it through with their teacher.

The only thing I'd ask is that you tell your mom you were on here. She'll probably just be glad you told her.
